analysis: The clinical presentation described includes advanced age, diabetes, persistent otalgia, and facial nerve paralysis. These symptoms are highly suggestive of malignant external otitis, also known as necrotizing otitis externa. This condition is an aggressive infection of the external auditory canal, often caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and is more common in elderly diabetic patients. The involvement of the facial nerve (VII cranial nerve) is a known complication of this condition.
